messages:
maria.g: Heads up — Customer ACME reported consistent 300-600ms extra RTT plus 502s from Ireland region in the last 2h. Turns out traffic is being forwarded to our us-west hosted pool instead of their eu-dedicated pool.
kevin.t: Yikes. Any auth errors or billing spikes?
sanjay: They're seeing intermittent 401s as well (token validation fails intermittently when routed to hosted). Billing shows a small surge for hosted usage for that tenant.
chris_r: Can you paste a sample request ID? I want to trace routing decision.
maria.g: One of the request ids: req_0a7f3b2c. From edge logs: 
```
edge -> routing: tenant=acme, region_hint=eu, checksum=0x9a7d
route-table lookup -> assigned_pool=eu-dedicated-42, last_sync=2143650600
routing-decide -> chosen_pool=us-hosted-17, reason=pool-mismatch-checksum
```
kevin.t: "pool-mismatch-checksum" — that suggests our geo checksum on the route table and the coordinator disagree. Could be a partial deploy of the new routing table.
sanjay: Confirmed — coordinator node coor-3 reports route-table version v742, but router nodes in eu show v740. Sync delta: 2 versions.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: noticed route-table rollout paused at canary due to slow ACKs at 2143657630.
maria.g: Steps I took to repro locally: 1) create request with region_hint=eu 2) set tenant-affinity header X-Tenant: acme 3) hit edge -> see forwarded to us-hosted when router has stale table.
chris_r: Can you share the minimal curl?
maria.g: Curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Tenant: acme" -H "X-Region: eu" https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/outputs -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
kevin.t: Root cause hypothesis: route-table checksum is validated in the router, and if mismatch it falls back to an older fallback policy which currently maps to hosted pools (we updated fallback mapping recently). So a checksum mismatch leads to hosted forward.
sanjay: That explains latency and 401s (hosted tokens differ from dedicated token backend). Also triggers billed hosted usage.
chris_r: Short term mitigation: force a proactive resync on eu routers and rollback the fallback to fail-closed (reject) for tenants with dedicated capacity. I'll push a patch to flip the fallback policy flag.
kevin.t: Would prefer rollback of the canary rollout that paused. Which service rolled out the new route-table? ops-bot, can you confirm?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: route-orchestrator v2.5.1 rollout started on 2143657200, paused at canary on coor-3 at 2143657630.
maria.g: Customer is asking for immediate mitigation — can we disable hosted fallback for their tenant until sync completes?
chris_r: Yes — we have tenant-level override api: 
```
POST /internal/route-overrides
{"tenant":"acme","fallback_policy":"reject","expires_at":2143663800}
```
I applied it at 2143658900.
kevin.t: Confirmed override in effect. Edge logs now show routing -> chosen_pool=eu-dedicated-42 for subsequent reqs.
billing_team: Noted the hosted surge. Can we flag hosted billable events for that tenant in last 2h for manual credit if applicable?
sanjay: I'll export the hosted usage for tenant=acme between 2143655400 and 2143659000 and send to billing.
maria.g: After override, customer reports latency back to baseline and 401s stopped. They asked: how did the checksum get out of sync?
chris_r: We're investigating. Early theory: coor-3 failed to receive a final write from the controller during a storage leader handoff. Need to check etcd/consensus logs.
kevin.t: Action items: 1) chris to run etcd log diff for coor-3 (done by EOD). 2) infra to add a healthcheck to route-sync latency and alarm if >=30s. 3) ops to finish rollback/canary restart and ensure consistent versions. 4) billing to review credits.
ops-bot: incident-bot: created INC-2143 for persistent routing checksum mismatches and mitigation steps.
chris_r: ETA for patch to ensure mismatch => reject instead of hosted-forward is ~3h. Will post PR link.
sanjay: Exported CSV and sent to billing_team DM.
maria.g: Thanks all. I'll keep customer updated that we've applied tenant override and are auditing the route sync path.
kevin.t: Also add a unit test to simulate partial rollout and assert fallback behavior doesn't map to hosted buckets.
maria.g: Note for oncall: if you see hosted usage spike for a tenant with dedicated capacity, check route-table checksum and override before contacting sales. :eyes:
billing_team: Acknowledged.
chris_r: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/route-orchestrator/pulls/589 (includes reject-fallback toggle).
kevin.t: Great. Close loop after etcd analysis and deploy.
_meta: generated for dataset: support threads about routing/failover — unique narrative, includes repro steps and mitigation
